page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, ensuring dedicated CPU allocation with exactly one thread per physical core.

This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps. The arm64 CPU architecture requires compatible software builds, which represents a key operational tradeoff compared to traditional x86-64 environments. Additionally, the lack of hyperthreading means each of the 32 vCPUs maps directly to a dedicated physical core, providing predictable execution times for compute-bound tasks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton-based architecture is designed to deliver high resource density and compute throughput per unit of power compared to traditional architectures. The c9g.8xlarge is configured for workloads requiring high CPU-to-memory ratios, such as distributed analytics, batch processing, high-performance web serving, video encoding, and scientific modeling.
